integrity: Exact universal argument and standalone finite exact-enumeration checker; finite checks do not establish the infinite assertion. General graph-spread integrality and Cartesian tensorization are acknowledged prior facts; no claim of independent validation.
limitations: Two complete-graph factors each have at least three vertices; ordinary unweighted categorical graph product; uniform vertex measure; real one-Lipschitz functions; quadratic centered L2 norm only. Neither weighted products nor other graph-product families are covered. Literature equivalence risk remains.
title: Sharp Lipschitz variance and a three-regime transition on categorical products of cliques
